abw.title: Aruba
abw.extract: Aruba, officially the Country of Aruba, is an island constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, in the southern Caribbean Sea 29 kilometres (18 mi) north of the Venezuelan peninsula of Paraguaná and 80 kilometres (50 mi) north-west of Curaçao. In 1986, Aruba became a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands and acquired the official name.

abw-x01.title: Aruba
abw-x01.extract: Aruba, officially the Country of Aruba, is an island constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, in the southern Caribbean Sea 29 kilometres (18 mi) north of the Venezuelan peninsula of Paraguaná and 80 kilometres (50 mi) north-west of Curaçao. In 1986, Aruba became a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands and acquired the official name.

aia.title: Anguilla
aia.extract: Anguilla is a British Overseas Territory of the Caribbean region in the North Atlantic Ocean. It is one of the most northerly of the Leeward Islands in the Lesser Antilles, lying east of Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands and directly north of Saint Martin.

aia-x01.title: Blowing Point, Anguilla
aia-x01.extract: Blowing Point is a village and one of the fourteen Districts of Anguila, located on the southern coast. It is home to Anguilla's ferry terminal.

aia-x02.title: East End, Anguilla
aia-x02.extract: East End is one of the fourteen Districts of Anguilla.  Its population at the 2011 census was 671.

aia-x03.title: George Hill, Anguilla
aia-x03.extract: George Hill is one of the fourteen Districts of Anguilla.  Its population at the 2011 census was 879.

aia-x04.title: Island Harbour, Anguilla
aia-x04.extract: Island Harbour is one of the fourteen Districts of Anguilla.  Its population at the 2011 census was 988.

aia-x05.title: North Hill, Anguilla
aia-x05.extract: North Hill is one of the fourteen Districts of Anguilla.  Its population at the 2011 census was 464.

aia-x06.title: North Side, Anguilla
aia-x06.extract: North Side is one of the fourteen districts of Anguilla, a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean. It covers both coastal and inland areas on the northeastern coast of the main island.

aia-x07.title: Sandy Ground, Anguilla
aia-x07.extract: Sandy Ground is a village and one of the fourteen Districts of Anguilla, and its  main port. The long curved beach is backed by high cliffs and a disused salt pond.

aia-x08.title: Sandy Hill, Anguilla
aia-x08.extract: Sandy Hill is one of the fourteen Districts of Anguilla.  Its population at the 2011 census was 636.

aia-x09.title: South Hill, Anguilla
aia-x09.extract: South Hill is one of the fourteen Districts of Anguilla.  Its population at the 2011 census was 1,722.

aia-x10.title: Stoney Ground
aia-x10.extract: Stoney Ground is one of the fourteen Districts of Anguilla.  Its population at the 2011 census was 1,549.

aia-x11.title: The Farrington
aia-x11.extract: The Farrington is one of the fourteen districts of Anguilla.  Its population at the 2011 census was 624.

aia-x12.title: The Quarter, Anguilla
aia-x12.extract: The Quarter is one of the fourteen Districts of Anguilla.  Its population at the 2011 census was 959.

aia-x13.title: The Valley, Anguilla
aia-x13.extract: The Valley is the capital of Anguilla, one of its fourteen districts, and the main town on the island. As of 2011, it had a population of 3,269.

aia-x14.title: West End, Anguilla
aia-x14.extract: West End is one of the fourteen Districts of Anguilla.  Its population at the 2011 census was 813.

atg.title: Antigua and Barbuda
atg.extract: Antigua and Barbuda is an archipelagic country in the Caribbean composed of Antigua, Barbuda, and dozens of other small islands. Antigua and Barbuda has a total area of 440 km2 (170 sq mi), making it one of the smallest countries in the Caribbean.

atg-03.title: Saint George, Antigua and Barbuda
atg-03.extract: Saint George (Antiguan and Barbudan Creole: Sen Jaaj), officially the Parish of Saint George, is a parish of Antigua and Barbuda on the island of Antigua. Saint George borders Saint Peter to the southeast, and Saint John to the west and south.

atg-04.title: Saint John, Antigua and Barbuda
atg-04.extract: Saint John (Antiguan and Barbudan Creole: Sen Jaan), officially the Parish of Saint John, is a civil parish of Antigua and Barbuda, on the northwestern portion of Antigua island. Its capital is the city of St.

atg-05.title: Saint Mary, Antigua and Barbuda
atg-05.extract: Saint Mary (South Antiguan Creole: Sen Mieree), officially the Parish of Saint Mary, is a parish of Antigua and Barbuda on the island of Antigua. Saint Mary borders Saint John to the north, and Saint Paul to the east.

atg-06.title: Saint Paul, Antigua and Barbuda
atg-06.extract: Saint Paul (Antiguan and Barbudan Creole: Sen Paal), officially the Parish of Saint Paul, is a parish of Antigua and Barbuda on the island of Antigua. It had an estimated population of 9,004 in 2018.

atg-07.title: Saint Peter, Antigua and Barbuda
atg-07.extract: Saint Peter (Antiguan and Barbudan Creole: Sen Peeta), officially the Parish of Saint Peter, is a parish of Antigua and Barbuda on the island of Antigua. Saint Peter borders Saint Paul to the south, Saint Philip to the east, and Saint George and Saint John to the west.

atg-08.title: Saint Philip, Antigua and Barbuda
atg-08.extract: Saint Philip (Antiguan and Barbudan Creole: Sen Filip), officially the Parish of Saint Philip, is a civil parish of Antigua and Barbuda, on the easternmost portion of Antigua island. Its capital is the village of St.

atg-10.title: Barbuda
atg-10.extract: Barbuda (; Barbudan Creole: Baabyuuda) is an island and dependency located in the eastern Caribbean forming part of the twin-island state of Antigua and Barbuda as an autonomous entity. Barbuda is located approximately 30 miles (48 km) north of Antigua.

atg-11.title: Redonda
atg-11.extract: Redonda (Antiguan and Barbudan Creole: Radonda  or Radawnda) is an uninhabited Caribbean island which is a dependency of Saint John, Antigua and Barbuda, in the Leeward Islands, West Indies. The island is about 1.6 kilometres (1 mi) long, 0.5 kilometres (0.3 mi) wide, and is 296 metres (971 ft) high at its highest point.

bhs.title: The Bahamas
bhs.extract: The Bahamas, officially the Commonwealth of The Bahamas, is an archipelagic country in the Caribbean located within the Lucayan Archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean. The country comprises 700 islands, and more than 2,500 cays in the Atlantic Ocean, located north of Cuba and north-west of the island of Hispaniola (split between the Dominican Republic and Haiti) and the Turks and Caicos Islands, southeast of the US state of Florida and east of the Florida Keys.

bhs-ak.title: Acklins
bhs-ak.extract:
Acklins is an island and district of the Bahamas.
It is one of a group of islands arranged along a large, shallow lagoon called the Bight of Acklins, of which the largest are Crooked Island (200 km2 or 76 sq mi) in the north and Acklins (310 km2 or 120 sq mi) in the southeast, and the smaller are Long Cay (once known as Fortune Island, (21 km2 or 8 sq mi)) in the northwest, and Castle Island in the south.

bhs-bi.title: Bimini
bhs-bi.extract: Bimini () is the westernmost district of the Bahamas and comprises a chain of islands located about 80 kilometres (50 mi) due east of Miami. Bimini is the closest point in the Bahamas to the mainland United States and approximately 210 km (130 mi) west-northwest of Nassau.

bhs-bp.title: Black Point, Bahamas
bhs-bp.extract: Black Point is one of the districts of the Bahamas. As of 2010, it has a population of 414 and an area of 12.1 km2.

bhs-by.title: Berry Islands
bhs-by.extract:
The Berry Islands are a chain of islands and a district of The Bahamas, covering about twelve square miles (31 km2).
The Berry Islands consist of about thirty islands and over one hundred small islands or cays, often referred to as "The Fish Bowl of The Bahamas." They have a population of 1,002 (2022 census), most of whom are on Great Harbour Cay.

bhs-ce.title: Central Eleuthera
bhs-ce.extract:
Central Eleuthera is one of 31 administrative districts in the Bahamas, and 5 on the island of Eleuthera.
Its capital, Governor's Harbour, is the largest city in the district, with a population of 701.

bhs-ci.title: Cat Island, Bahamas
bhs-ci.extract: Cat Island is located in the Bahamas, and is one of its districts.  Cat Island also has the nation's highest point, Mount Alvernia (formerly known as Como Hill).

bhs-ck.title: Crooked Island, Bahamas
bhs-ck.extract: Crooked Island is an island and district, part of a group of Bahamian islands defining a large, shallow lagoon called the Bight of Acklins, of which the largest are Crooked Island in the north and Acklins in the south-east, and the smaller are Long Cay (once known as Fortune Island) in the north-west, and Castle Island in the south.

bhs-co.title: Central Abaco
bhs-co.extract: Central Abaco is an administrative district of the Bahamas. It is part of the larger  Abaco Islands chain and is the largest Schedule 2 district in the Bahamas.

bhs-cs.title: Central Andros
bhs-cs.extract: Central Andros is one of the districts of the Bahamas, on Andros Island. Its current Chief Councillor is Ms.

bhs-eg.title: East Grand Bahama
bhs-eg.extract:
East Grand Bahama is a district of The Bahamas, situated on the eastern part of the island of Grand Bahama, with a population collectively of 11,411 people.
The local government seat for the district is in the settlement of High Rock, a fairly small town.

bhs-ex.title: Exuma
bhs-ex.extract:
Exuma is a district of the Bahamas, consisting of over 365 islands and cays.
The largest of the islands is Great Exuma, which is 37 mi (60 km) in length and connected to another island, Little Exuma, by a small bridge.

bhs-fp.title: Freeport, Bahamas
bhs-fp.extract: Freeport is a city, district and free trade zone on the island of Grand Bahama in the northwest part of The Bahamas. In 1955, Wallace Groves, a Virginian financier with lumber interests in Grand Bahama, was granted 20,000 hectares (50,000 acres) of pineyard with substantial areas of swamp and scrubland by the Bahamian government with a mandate to economically develop the area.

bhs-hi.title: Harbour Island, Bahamas
bhs-hi.extract: Harbour Island is an island and administrative district in the Bahamas located off the northeast coast of Eleuthera Island. Harbour Island, Jacobs Island, Man Island, Pierre Island and others form what looks like a reef that encloses the east and north sides of a lagoon in the northeast corner of Eleuthera.

bhs-in.title: Inagua
bhs-in.extract: Inagua is the southernmost district of the Bahamas, comprising the islands of Great Inagua and Little Inagua. The headquarters for the district council are in Matthew Town.

bhs-li.title: Long Island, Bahamas
bhs-li.extract: Long Island is an island in The Bahamas that is split by the Tropic of Cancer. It is one of the Districts of the Bahamas and is known as the most scenic island in the Bahamas.

bhs-mc.title: Mangrove Cay
bhs-mc.extract: Mangrove Cay is one of the districts of the Bahamas on Andros. The capital of Mangrove Cay is Moxey Town in the northeast corner of the island.

bhs-mi.title: Moore's Island
bhs-mi.extract:
Moore's Island is one of the districts of the Bahamas, on the Abaco Islands.
Moore's Island is a cay, 28 miles (45 km) to the west of the main island of Abaco.

bhs-ne.title: North Eleuthera
bhs-ne.extract: North Eleuthera is one of the districts of the Bahamas, on the island of Eleuthera. It had a  population of 3,247 in 2010.

bhs-no.title: North Abaco
bhs-no.extract: North Abaco is one of the districts of the Bahamas, on the Abaco Islands. It has a population of 9,578 according to the 2010 census.

bhs-ns.title: North Andros
bhs-ns.extract: North Andros is one of the 31 districts of the Bahamas. It is also the largest district (in area) in the country, and has some of the largest settlements in Andros Island.

bhs-rc.title: Rum Cay
bhs-rc.extract: Rum Cay (formerly known as Mamana and Santa Maria de la Concepción) is an island and district of The Bahamas. It measures 30 square miles (78 km2) in area.

bhs-ri.title: Ragged Island, Bahamas
bhs-ri.extract: Ragged Island is a 23 km2 (8.9 mi2) island and district in the southern Bahamas. Ragged Island is part of the Jumentos Cays and Ragged Island Chain.

bhs-sa.title: South Andros
bhs-sa.extract:
South Andros is a district of the nation of the Bahamas.
Geographically, South Andros is the southernmost third of the land mass colloquially called Andros, which includes the districts of North Andros, Central Andros, Mangrove Cay and South Andros.

bhs-se.title: South Eleuthera
bhs-se.extract:
South Eleuthera is one of the districts of the Bahamas, on the island of Eleuthera.
The district had a population of 4,955 in 2010.

bhs-so.title: South Abaco
bhs-so.extract:
South Abaco is one of the districts of the Bahamas, on the Abaco Islands.
The district had a population of 7,646 in 2010.

bhs-ss.title: San Salvador Island
bhs-ss.extract: San Salvador Island, previously Watling's Island, is an island and district of the Bahamas, famed for being the probable location of Christopher Columbus's first landing of the Americas on 12 October 1492 during his first voyage. This historical importance, the island's tropical beaches, and its proximity to the United States have made tourism central to the local economy.

bhs-sw.title: Spanish Wells
bhs-sw.extract: Spanish Wells is a district of the Bahamas. The settlement consists of a medium-sized town on the island of St.

bhs-wg.title: West Grand Bahama
bhs-wg.extract: West Grand Bahama is one of 31 districts of the Bahamas. The district covers the entire western portion of Grand Bahama island, excluding the city of Freeport, which forms its own district.

bhs-x01.title: New Providence
bhs-x01.extract: New Providence is the most populous island in the Bahamas. On the eastern side of the island is the national capital city of Nassau; it had a population of 246,329 at the 2010 Census, and a population of 292,522 at the 2022 census.

bjn.title: Bajo Nuevo Bank
bjn.extract: Bajo Nuevo Bank (Spanish: Bajo Nuevo), also known as the Petrel Islands (Spanish: Islas Petrel), is an uninhabited reef with some grass-covered islets in the western Caribbean Sea. The closest neighboring land feature is Serranilla Bank, located 110 kilometres (68 miles) to the west.

blm.extract: Saint Barthélemy, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint Barthélemy, also known as St. Barts and St.

blm-x00.extract: Saint Barthélemy, officially the Territorial Collectivity of Saint Barthélemy, also known as St. Barts and St.

blz.title: Belize
blz.extract: Belize is a country on the north-eastern coast of Central America. It is bordered by Mexico to the north, the Caribbean Sea to the east, and Guatemala to the west and south.

blz-bz.title: Belize District
blz-bz.extract: Belize is a district of the nation of Belize. Its capital is Belize City.

blz-cy.title: Cayo District
blz-cy.extract: Cayo is a district located in the west part of Belize, and it contains the capital, Belmopan. It is the most extensive, second-most populous and third-most densely populated of the six districts of Belize.

blz-czl.title: Corozal District
blz-czl.extract: Corozal is the northernmost district of the nation of Belize. The population was 46,071 in 2024.

blz-ow.title: Orange Walk District
blz-ow.extract: Orange Walk is a district in the northwest of the nation of Belize, with its district capital in Orange Walk Town.

blz-sc.title: Stann Creek District
blz-sc.extract: Stann Creek is a district in the south east region of Belize. According to the 2022 census, the district had a population of 48,162 people.

blz-tol.title: Toledo District
blz-tol.extract: Toledo is the southernmost and least populated district in Belize. Punta Gorda is the District capital.

bmu.title: Bermuda
bmu.extract: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory in the North Atlantic Ocean. The closest land outside the territory is in the US state of North Carolina, about 1,035 km (643 mi) to the west-northwest.

bqi.title: Navassa Island
bqi.extract: Navassa Island (; Haitian Creole: Lanavaz; French: Île de la Navasse, sometimes la Navase) is an uninhabited island in the Windward Passage of the Caribbean Sea. Located east of Jamaica, south of Cuba, and 40 nautical miles (74 km; 46 mi) west of Jérémie on the Tiburon Peninsula of Haiti, it is subject to an ongoing territorial dispute between Haiti and the United States, the latter of which administers the island through the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

bqi-76.title: Navassa Island
bqi-76.extract: Navassa Island (; Haitian Creole: Lanavaz; French: Île de la Navasse, sometimes la Navase) is an uninhabited island in the Windward Passage of the Caribbean Sea. Located east of Jamaica, south of Cuba, and 40 nautical miles (74 km; 46 mi) west of Jérémie on the Tiburon Peninsula of Haiti, it is subject to an ongoing territorial dispute between Haiti and the United States, the latter of which administers the island through the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

brb.title: Barbados
brb.extract: Barbados is an island nation in the Caribbean Sea. It is part of the Lesser Antilles of the West Indies and is the southernmost and easternmost island of the Caribbean region.

brb-01.title: Christ Church, Barbados
brb-01.extract: The parish of Christ Church is one of eleven in Barbados. It has a land area of 57 km2 (22 sq mi) and is found at the southern end of the island.

brb-02.title: Saint Andrew, Barbados
brb-02.extract: St. Andrew is one of eleven parishes of Barbados.

brb-03.title: Saint George, Barbados
brb-03.extract: St. George is a parish of Barbados.

brb-04.title: Saint James, Barbados
brb-04.extract: The parish of St. James is located in the western central part of the country of Barbados.

brb-05.title: Saint John, Barbados
brb-05.extract: The parish of  St. John in Barbados is on the eastern side of the island.

brb-06.title: Saint Joseph, Barbados
brb-06.extract: The parish of St. Joseph in Barbados is on the eastern side of the island.

brb-07.title: Saint Lucy, Barbados
brb-07.extract: The parish of St. Lucy is the northernmost in the country of Barbados.

brb-08.title: Saint Michael, Barbados
brb-08.extract: The parish of St. Michael is one of 11 parishes in Barbados.

brb-09.title: Saint Peter, Barbados
brb-09.extract: The parish of St. Peter is one of eleven in the Caribbean island country of Barbados.

brb-10.title: Saint Philip, Barbados
brb-10.extract: Saint Philip is a parish of Barbados at the easternmost end of the island. Saint Philip’s Parish Church was built as the Anglican parish church in 1640.

brb-11.title: Saint Thomas, Barbados
brb-11.extract: The landlocked parish of St. Thomas is in the centre of Barbados.

can.title: Canada
can.extract: Canada is a country in North America. Its ten provinces and three territories extend from the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean and northward into the Arctic Ocean, making it the second-largest country by total area, with the longest coastline of any country.

can-ab.title: Alberta
can-ab.extract: Alberta is a province in Western Canada and is one of the three prairie provinces. Alberta is bordered by British Columbia to its west, Saskatchewan to its east, the Northwest Territories to its north, and the U.S. state of Montana to its south.

can-mb.title: Manitoba
can-mb.extract: Manitoba is a province of Canada at the longitudinal centre of the country. It is Canada's fifth-most populous province, with an estimated population of 1,517,379 as of 2026.

can-nb.title: New Brunswick
can-nb.extract: New Brunswick is a province of Canada. It borders Quebec to the northwest, the Gulf of Saint Lawrence to the northeast, Nova Scotia to the east, the Bay of Fundy to the southeast, and the U.S. state of Maine to the southwest.

can-nl.title: Newfoundland and Labrador
can-nl.extract: Newfoundland and Labrador is the easternmost province of Canada, in the country's Atlantic region. It comprises the island of Newfoundland and the continental region of Labrador, with an area of 405,212 km2 (156,453 sq mi) and a population of 552,462 in 2026.

can-ns.title: Nova Scotia
can-ns.extract: Nova Scotia is a province in The Maritimes region of Canada, located on the nation's east coast. With an estimated population of over 1 million as of 2026, Nova Scotia is the most populous province in Atlantic Canada.

can-nt.title: Northwest Territories
can-nt.extract: The Northwest Territories is a territory of Canada. At a land area of approximately 1,127,711.92 square kilometres (435,412.01 sq mi) and a 2026 estimated population of 45,904, it is the second-largest and second-most populous of the three territories in Northern Canada.

can-nu.title: Nunavut
can-nu.extract: Nunavut is the largest and northernmost territory of Canada. It was separated from the Northwest Territories in 1999, via the Nunavut Act and the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement Act, which provided this territory to the Inuit for self-government.

can-on.title: Ontario
can-on.extract: Ontario is the southernmost province of Canada. Located in Central Canada, Ontario is the country's most populous province.

can-qc.title: Quebec
can-qc.extract: Quebec (French: Québec) is Canada's largest province by area. Located in Central Canada, it is the country's only Francophone-majority province.

can-sk.title: Saskatchewan
can-sk.extract: Saskatchewan is a province in Western Canada. It is bordered to the west by Alberta, to the north by the Northwest Territories, to the east by Manitoba, to the northeast by Nunavut, and to the south by the United States (Montana and North Dakota).

can-yt.title: Yukon
can-yt.extract: Yukon (, Canadian French: [jukõ]) is a territory of Canada, bordering British Columbia to the south, the Northwest Territories to the east, the Beaufort Sea to the north, and the U.S. state of Alaska to the west. It is Canada's westernmost and smallest territory by land area.

cri.title: Costa Rica
cri.extract: Costa Rica, officially the Republic of Costa Rica, is a country in Central America. It borders Nicaragua to the north, the Caribbean Sea to the northeast, Panama to the southeast, and the Pacific Ocean to the southwest, sharing a maritime border with Ecuador to the south of Cocos Island.

cri-a.title: Alajuela Province
cri-a.extract: Alajuela (Spanish pronunciation: [alaˈxwela]) is a province of Costa Rica. It is located in the north-central part of the country, bordering Nicaragua to the north.

cri-c.title: Cartago Province
cri-c.extract: Cartago (Spanish pronunciation: [kaɾˈtaɣo]), which means Carthage in Spanish, is a province of central Costa Rica. It is one of the smallest provinces, however probably the richest of the Spanish Colonial era sites and traditions.

cri-g.title: Guanacaste Province
cri-g.extract: Guanacaste (Spanish pronunciation: [ɡwanaˈkaste]) is a province of Costa Rica in the northwestern part of the country, along the coast of the Pacific Ocean. It is bordered by Nicaragua to the north, Alajuela Province to the east, and Puntarenas Province to the southeast.

cri-h.title: Heredia Province
cri-h.extract: Heredia (Spanish pronunciation: [eˈɾeðja]) is a province of Costa Rica. It is in the north-central part of the country.

cri-l.title: Limón Province
cri-l.extract: Limón (Spanish pronunciation: [liˈmon]) is one of seven provinces in Costa Rica. The province covers an area of 9,176.96 km2, and has a population of 386,862.

cri-p.title: Puntarenas Province
cri-p.extract: Puntarenas (Spanish pronunciation: [puntaˈɾenas]) is a province of Costa Rica. It is located in the western part of the country, covering most of Costa Rica's Pacific Ocean coast, and it is the largest province in Costa Rica.

cri-sj.title: San José Province
cri-sj.extract: San José (Spanish pronunciation: [saŋ xoˈse]) is a province of Costa Rica. It is located in the central part of the country, and borders (clockwise beginning in the north) the provinces of Alajuela, Heredia, Limón, Cartago and Puntarenas.

cub.title: Cuba
cub.extract: Cuba, officially the Republic of Cuba, is an island country in the Caribbean. It comprises the eponymous main island as well as 4,195 islands, islets, and cays.

cub-01.title: Pinar del Río Province
cub-01.extract: The Pinar del Río Province is one of the 15 provinces of Cuba.  It is at the western end of the island of Cuba.

cub-03.title: Havana
cub-03.extract: Havana ( hə-VAN-ə, US also  hə-VAH-nə; Spanish: La Habana [la aˈβana] ) is the capital and largest city of Cuba. The heart of La Habana Province, Havana is the country's main port and commercial center.

cub-04.title: Matanzas Province
cub-04.extract: Matanzas (Latin American Spanish pronunciation: [maˈtansas]) is one of the provinces of Cuba.  Major towns in the province include Cárdenas, Colón, Jovellanos and the capital of the same name, Matanzas.

cub-05.title: Villa Clara Province
cub-05.extract: Villa Clara is one of the provinces of Cuba.  It is located in the central region of the island bordering on the Atlantic Ocean to the north, Matanzas Province to the west, Sancti Spiritus Province to the east, and Cienfuegos Province to the South.

cub-06.title: Cienfuegos Province
cub-06.extract: Cienfuegos (Spanish pronunciation: [sjeɱˈfweɣos]) is one of the provinces of Cuba. The capital city of the province is also called Cienfuegos and was founded by French settlers in 1819.

cub-07.title: Sancti Spíritus Province
cub-07.extract: Sancti Spíritus (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈsaŋktjesˈpiɾitus]) is one of the provinces of Cuba. Its capital is the identically named Sancti Spíritus.

cub-08.title: Ciego de Ávila Province
cub-08.extract: Ciego de Ávila (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈsjeɣo ðe ˈaβila]) is one of the provinces of Cuba, and was previously part of Camagüey Province.  Its capital is Ciego de Ávila, which lies on the Carretera Central (central highway), and the second city is Morón, further north.

cub-09.title: Camagüey Province
cub-09.extract: Camagüey (Spanish pronunciation: [kamaˈ(ɣ)wej]) is the largest of the provinces of Cuba.  Its capital is Camagüey.

cub-10.title: Las Tunas Province
cub-10.extract: Las Tunas is one of the provinces of Cuba. Major towns include Puerto Padre, Amancio, and the capital city, Las Tunas (historically Victoria de Las Tunas).

cub-11.title: Holguín Province
cub-11.extract: Holguín (Spanish pronunciation: [olˈɣin]) is one of the provinces of Cuba, the third most populous after Havana and Santiago de Cuba.  It lies in the southeast of the country.

cub-12.title: Granma Province
cub-12.extract: Granma is one of the provinces of Cuba. Its capital is Bayamo.

cub-13.title: Santiago de Cuba Province
cub-13.extract: Santiago de Cuba Province is the second most populated province in the island of Cuba. The largest city Santiago de Cuba is the main administrative center.

cub-14.title: Guantánamo Province
cub-14.extract: Guantánamo is the easternmost province of Cuba. Its capital is also called Guantánamo.

cub-15.title: Artemisa Province
cub-15.extract: Artemisa Province is one of the two new provinces created from the former La Habana Province, whose creation was approved by the Cuban National Assembly on August 1, 2010, the other being Mayabeque Province. The new provinces came into existence on January 1, 2011.

cub-16.title: Mayabeque Province
cub-16.extract: Mayabeque Province is one of two new provinces created from the former La Habana Province, whose creation was approved by the Cuban National Assembly on August 1, 2010, the other being Artemisa Province. The new provinces came in to existence on January 1, 2011.

cub-99.title: Isla de la Juventud
cub-99.extract: Isla de la Juventud (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈizla ðe la xuβenˈtuð]; lit. 'Isle of Youth') is the second-largest Cuban island (after Cuba's mainland) and the seventh-largest island in the West Indies (after mainland Cuba, Hispaniola, Jamaica, Puerto Rico, Trinidad, and Andros Island). The island was called the Isle of Pines (Spanish: Isla de Pinos) until 1978.

cuw.title: Curaçao
cuw.extract: Curaçao, officially the Country of Curaçao, is a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. It is an island country located in the southern Caribbean Sea, specifically the Dutch Caribbean region, about 65 km (40 mi) north of Venezuela and 80 km (50 mi) southeast of Aruba.

cuw-x01.title: Curaçao
cuw-x01.extract: Curaçao, officially the Country of Curaçao, is a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands. It is an island country located in the southern Caribbean Sea, specifically the Dutch Caribbean region, about 65 km (40 mi) north of Venezuela and 80 km (50 mi) southeast of Aruba.

cym.title: Cayman Islands
cym.extract: The Cayman Islands () is a self-governing British Overseas Territory in the western Caribbean. With a population of over 90,000, it is the most populated of all the British Overseas Territories.

dma.title: Dominica
dma.extract: Dominica officially the Commonwealth of Dominica, is an island country in the Caribbean. It is part of the Windward Islands chain in the Lesser Antilles archipelago in the Caribbean Sea.

dma-02.title: Saint Andrew Parish, Dominica
dma-02.extract: Saint Andrew is one of Dominica's 10 administrative parishes. It is bordered by St.

dma-03.title: Saint David Parish, Dominica
dma-03.extract: Saint David is one of Dominica's ten administrative parishes, located on the eastern side of the island. It is bordered by St.

dma-04.title: Saint George Parish, Dominica
dma-04.extract: Saint George is one of Dominica's 10 administrative parishes. It is bordered by Saint Paul and part of the Boeri River (to the north), Saint David and Saint Patrick (to the east), Saint Luke (to the south).

dma-05.title: Saint John Parish, Dominica
dma-05.extract: Saint John is one of Dominica's 10 administrative parishes. It is bordered by St.

dma-06.extract: Saint Joseph is one of Dominica's 10 administrative parishes. It is bordered by St.

dma-07.title: Saint Luke Parish, Dominica
dma-07.extract: Saint Luke is one of Dominica's 10 administrative parishes. It is bordered by St.

dma-08.title: Saint Mark Parish, Dominica
dma-08.extract: Saint Mark is one of Dominica's ten administrative parishes (Dominica is in the Lesser Antilles). It is bordered by St.

dma-09.title: Saint Patrick Parish, Dominica
dma-09.extract: Saint Patrick is one of Dominica's 10 administrative parishes. It is bordered by St.

dma-10.extract: Saint Paul is one of Dominica's 10 administrative parishes. It is bordered by St.

dma-11.extract: Saint Peter is one of Dominica's 10 administrative parishes. It is bordered by St.

dom.title: Dominican Republic
dom.extract: The Dominican Republic is an island country on the eastern part of the Caribbean island of Hispaniola in the Greater Antilles of the Caribbean Sea in the North Atlantic Ocean. It shares a maritime border with Puerto Rico to the east and a land border with Haiti to the west, occupying the eastern five-eighths of Hispaniola which, along with Saint Martin, is one of only two islands in the Caribbean shared by two sovereign states.

dom-01.title: Distrito Nacional
dom-01.extract: Distrito Nacional (D.N.; pronounced [disˈtɾito nasjoˈnal], locally [dihˈtɾito nasjoˈnal]; lit. 'National District') is a subdivision of the Dominican Republic enclosing the capital Santo Domingo. It is not in any of the provinces, but in practice, it acts as a province on its own.

dom-02.title: Azua Province
dom-02.extract: Azua (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈaswa]) is a province which is collectively one of the thirty-two provinces of the Dominican Republic. It is divided into 10 municipalities (the same as Santiago) and its capital city is Azua de Compostela.

dom-03.title: Baoruco Province
dom-03.extract: Baoruco, alternatively spelt Bahoruco (Spanish pronunciation: [baoˈɾuko]), is a province of the Dominican Republic. It is spread over an area of 1,284.9 km2 (496.1 sq mi), and has its capital at Neiba.

dom-04.title: Barahona Province
dom-04.extract: Barahona (Spanish pronunciation: [baɾaˈona]) is a province of the Dominican Republic. It is spread over an area of 1,768.71 km2 (682.90 sq mi), and has its capital at Santa Cruz de Barahona.

dom-05.title: Dajabón Province
dom-05.extract: Dajabón (Spanish pronunciation: [daxaˈβon]) is a northwestern province which currently comprises one of the 32 provinces of the Dominican Republic. It is divided into 5 municipalities and its capital city with the same name.

dom-06.title: Duarte Province
dom-06.extract: Duarte (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈdwaɾte]) is a northeastern province which comprises one of the 32 provinces of the Dominican Republic. It is divided into 7 municipalities and its capital city is San Francisco de Macorís.

dom-08.title: El Seibo Province
dom-08.extract: El Seibo (Spanish pronunciation: [el ˈsejβo]), alternatively spelt El Seybo, is a province of the Dominican Republic. Before 1992 it included what is now Hato Mayor province.

dom-09.title: Espaillat Province
dom-09.extract: Espaillat (Spanish pronunciation: [espajˈʝat], locally [ehpajˈʝat]) is a province in the Dominican Republic. Located in the north central part of the country, it is spread over an area of 843 km2 (325 sq mi), and has its capital at Moca.

dom-10.title: Independencia Province
dom-10.extract: Independencia (Spanish pronunciation: [indepenˈdensja]) is a province of the Dominican Republic. It is spread over an area of 2,007.4 km2 (775.1 sq mi), and has its capital at Jimaní.

dom-11.title: La Altagracia Province
dom-11.extract: La Altagracia (Spanish pronunciation: [la altaˈɣɾasja]) is a province located in the eastern part of the Dominican Republic. It is the only region that borders the Atlantic Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.

dom-12.title: La Romana Province
dom-12.extract: La Romana (Spanish pronunciation: [la ɾoˈmana]) is a province of the Dominican Republic. The capital is also named La Romana, and is the third-largest city in the country.

dom-13.title: La Vega Province
dom-13.extract: La Vega (Spanish pronunciation: [la ˈβeɣa]) is one of the 32 provinces of the Dominican Republic. It is located in the Cibao Valley, the north-central region of the country, and is divided into 4 municipalities with its capital city being the namesake of La Vega.

dom-14.title: María Trinidad Sánchez Province
dom-14.extract: María Trinidad Sánchez (Spanish pronunciation: [maˈɾi.a tɾiniˈðað ˈsantʃes]) is a province of the Dominican Republic. It was split from Samaná Province in September 1959 as Julia Molina Province; in November 1961, it got its current name.

dom-15.title: Monte Cristi Province
dom-15.extract: Monte Cristi (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈmonte ˈkɾisti]), also spelled Montecristi is a province in the northwest of the Dominican Republic. The capital city is San Fernando de Monte Cristi (usually simply Monte Cristi).

dom-16.title: Pedernales Province
dom-16.extract: Pedernales (from Spanish 'flints'; pronounced [peðeɾˈnales]) is the southernmost province of the Dominican Republic, including the offshore island of Isla Beata. It was split from Barahona in 1957.

dom-17.title: Peravia Province
dom-17.extract: Peravia (Spanish pronunciation: [peˈɾaβja]) is a province in the southern region of the Dominican Republic. Located on the country's Caribbean coast which it is in the south, it is divided in 13 units (three municipalities and 10 municipal districts), while Baní is the province's capital.

dom-18.title: Puerto Plata Province
dom-18.extract: Puerto Plata (Spanish pronunciation: [pweɾtoˈplata], Silver Port); (French: Port-de-Plate) is a province in northern Dominican Republic. It is divided into 9 municipalities, 12 municipal districts and its capital is the resort city of the same name.

dom-19.title: Hermanas Mirabal Province
dom-19.extract: Hermanas Mirabal (Spanish pronunciation: [eɾˈmanas miɾaˈβal]; named after the Mirabal sisters) is a province of the Dominican Republic. It was split from Espaillat Province in 1952 and was originally called Salcedo, the name of its capital city; it is still referred to by this name sometimes.

dom-20.title: Samaná Province
dom-20.extract: Samaná (Spanish pronunciation: [samaˈna]) is a province of the Dominican Republic in the Samaná Peninsula located in the eastern region. Its capital is Santa Bárbara de Samaná, usually known as Samaná.

dom-21.title: San Cristóbal Province
dom-21.extract: San Cristóbal (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈsaŋ kɾisˈtoβal]) is a province in the southern region of Dominican Republic, located west of the capital Santo Domingo. With approximately 690,000 inhabitants (2022), it is the fourth most populated province in the country, only behind Santo Domingo, Santiago and the National District.

dom-22.title: San Juan Province (Dominican Republic)
dom-22.extract: San Juan (Spanish pronunciation: [saŋ ˈxwan]) is a province of the Dominican Republic. Established as Benefactor during the Age of Trujillo in 1938, it was renamed San Juan in 1961.

dom-23.title: San Pedro de Macorís Province
dom-23.extract: San Pedro de Macorís (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈsam ˈpeðɾo ðe makoˈɾis]) is a province of the Dominican Republic, also the name of its capital city. The city is fairly active due to its proximity to the national capital of Santo Domingo and also its role in the sugar industry.

dom-24.title: Sánchez Ramírez Province
dom-24.extract:
Sánchez Ramírez (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈsantʃes ɾaˈmiɾes]) 
It is spread over an area of 1,185.3 km2 (457.6 sq mi), and has its capital at Cotuí. It was established in 1952.

dom-25.title: Santiago Province (Dominican Republic)
dom-25.extract: Santiago (Spanish pronunciation: [sanˈtjaɣo]) is one of the 32 provinces of the Dominican Republic. It is divided into 10 municipalities and its capital city is Santiago de los Caballeros.

dom-26.title: Santiago Rodríguez Province
dom-26.extract: Santiago Rodríguez (Spanish pronunciation: [sanˈtjaɣo roˈðɾiɣes]) is a province in the northwest region of the Dominican Republic. It was split from Monte Cristi in 1948.

dom-27.title: Valverde Province
dom-27.extract: Valverde (Spanish pronunciation: [balˈβeɾðe]) is a province of the Dominican Republic. It was split from Santiago Province in 1959.

dom-28.title: Monseñor Nouel Province
dom-28.extract: Monseñor Nouel (Spanish pronunciation: [monseˈɲoɾ noˈwel]) is a province in the central region of the Dominican Republic. It was split from La Vega province in 1982.

dom-29.title: Monte Plata Province
dom-29.extract: Monte Plata (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈmonte ˈplata]) is an eastern province of the Dominican Republic, and also the name of its capital city. It was split from San Cristóbal in 1992.

dom-30.title: Hato Mayor Province
dom-30.extract: Hato Mayor (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈato maˈʝoɾ]) is a province of the Dominican Republic. It was split from El Seibo in 1984.

dom-31.title: San José de Ocoa Province
dom-31.extract: San José de Ocoa (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈsaŋ xoˈse ðe oˈko.a]) is a province in the Dominican Republic. It is spread over an area of 853.4 km2 (329.5 sq mi), and has its capital at San José de Ocoa.

dom-32.title: Santo Domingo Province
dom-32.extract: Santo Domingo (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈsanto ðoˈmiŋɡo]) is a province of the Dominican Republic. It was split from the Distrito Nacional on 16 October 2001.

glp.title: Guadeloupe
glp.extract: Guadeloupe is an overseas department and region of France in the Caribbean. It consists of six inhabited islands—Basse-Terre, Grande-Terre, Marie-Galante, La Désirade, and two Îles des Saintes—and 30 uninhabited islets and 3 inhabited islets.

glp-gp.title: Guadeloupe
glp-gp.extract: Guadeloupe is an overseas department and region of France in the Caribbean. It consists of six inhabited islands—Basse-Terre, Grande-Terre, Marie-Galante, La Désirade, and two Îles des Saintes—and 30 uninhabited islets and 3 inhabited islets.

grd.title: Grenada
grd.extract: Grenada is an archipelagic country of the West Indies in the eastern Caribbean Sea. The southernmost of the Windward Islands, Grenada is directly south of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and about 160 kilometres (100 miles) north of Trinidad and the South American mainland.

grd-01.title: Saint Andrew Parish, Grenada
grd-01.extract: Saint Andrew's is the largest parish in Grenada. The main town is Grenville, which is also Grenada's second largest town after St George's.

grd-02.title: Saint David Parish, Grenada
grd-02.extract: Saint David's Parish is the fourth-largest of the parishes of Grenada in the island's southeast. The parish's main town (largest village) is St.

grd-03.title: Saint George Parish, Grenada
grd-03.extract: Saint George is one of the parishes of Grenada, located on the south-western end of the island. The capital of Grenada, St.

grd-04.title: Saint John Parish, Grenada
grd-04.extract: Saint John is one of the parishes of Grenada. Its capital is Gouyave.

grd-05.title: Saint Mark Parish, Grenada
grd-05.extract: Saint Mark is a parish on the west coast of Grenada. It is the smallest parish on the island in terms of both area and population.

grd-06.title: Saint Patrick Parish, Grenada
grd-06.extract: Saint Patrick is one of the Catholic parishes of Grenada, covering the north of the country.

grd-10.title: Carriacou and Petite Martinique
grd-10.extract:
Carriacou and Petite Martinique, also known as the Southern Grenadines, is a dependency (part) of Grenada, lying north of Grenada island and south of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines in the Lesser Antilles.
Carriacou Island is the largest island of the Grenadines, an archipelago in the Windward Islands chain.

grl.title: Greenland
grl.extract: Greenland is an autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark and is the largest of the kingdom's three constituent parts by land area, the others being Denmark proper and the Faroe Islands. Citizens of Greenland are citizens of Denmark.

grl-grl-2738.title: Pituffik
grl-grl-2738.extract: Pituffik (meaning 'mooring place, place to tie something') is a former Inughuit settlement in North Star Bay, near Mount Dundas at the eastern end of Bylot Sound in northern Greenland. It was located on the plain that is now occupied by the runway of the U.S. Pituffik Space Base, formerly Thule Air Base.

grl-ku.title: Kujalleq
grl-ku.extract: Kujalleq (Greenlandic: Greenlandic pronunciation: [kujaɬːɜq̚], Danish: Syden, lit. 'The South') is a municipality on the southern tip of Greenland, operational from 1 January 2009. The administrative center of the municipality is in Qaqortoq (formerly called Julianehåb).

grl-qa.title: Qaasuitsup
grl-qa.extract: Qaasuitsup (Greenlandic pronunciation: [qaːsuitt͡sup̚], Place of Polar Darkness) was a municipality in Greenland, operational from 1 January 2009 to 31 December 2017. As of January 2015, its population was 17,168.

grl-qe.title: Qeqqata
grl-qe.extract: Qeqqata (Greenlandic pronunciation: [qɜqːata], Danish: Centrum, lit. 'Centre') is a municipality in western Greenland, operational from 1 January 2009. The municipality was named after its location in the central-western part of the country.

grl-sm.title: Sermersooq
grl-sm.extract: Sermersooq (Greenlandic pronunciation: [sɜm.mɜs.sɔːq̚]) is a municipality in Greenland, formed on 1 January 2009 from five previous, smaller municipalities, and is the largest municipality in the world by area. Its administrative seat is the city of Nuuk, the capital of Greenland, and it is the most populous municipality in the country, with 24,229 inhabitants as of January 2025.

grl-uo.title: Northeast Greenland National Park
grl-uo.extract: Northeast Greenland National Park (Greenlandic: Kalaallit Nunaanni nuna eqqissisimatitaq, Danish: Nordøstgrønlands Nationalpark) is the world's largest national park and the 10th largest protected area (the only larger protected areas consist mostly of sea). Established in 1974, the Northeast Greenland national park expanded to its present size in 1988.

gtm.title: Guatemala
gtm.extract: Guatemala, officially the Republic of Guatemala, is a country in northern Central America. It is bordered to the north and west by Mexico, to the northeast (in the adjacency zone) by Belize, to the east by Honduras, and to the southeast by El Salvador.

gtm-av.title: Alta Verapaz
gtm-av.extract: Alta Verapaz (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈalta βeɾaˈpas]) is a department in the north central part of Guatemala. The capital and chief city of the department is Cobán.

gtm-bv.title: Baja Verapaz Department
gtm-bv.extract: Baja Verapaz (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈbaxa βeɾaˈpas]) is a department in Guatemala. In 2018, the population of the department was 299,476.

gtm-cm.title: Chimaltenango Department
gtm-cm.extract: Chimaltenango is a department of Guatemala. The capital is Chimaltenango.

gtm-cq.title: Chiquimula Department
gtm-cq.extract: Chiquimula is one of the 22 departments of Guatemala, in Central America. The departmental capital is also called Chiquimula.

gtm-es.title: Escuintla Department
gtm-es.extract: Escuintla (Spanish pronunciation: [esˈkwintla]) is one of the 22 departments of Guatemala. The capital of the department is the city of Escuintla.

gtm-gu.title: Guatemala Department
gtm-gu.extract: Guatemala Department is one of the 22 departments of Guatemala.  The capital is Guatemala City, which also serves as the national capital.

gtm-hu.title: Huehuetenango Department
gtm-hu.extract: Huehuetenango (Spanish pronunciation: [w̝e.we.t̪eˈnãŋ.ɡo]) is one of the 22 departments of Guatemala. It is located in the western highlands and shares the borders with the Mexican state of Chiapas in the north and west; with El Quiché in the east, and Totonicapán, Quetzaltenango and San Marcos in the south.

gtm-iz.title: Izabal Department
gtm-iz.extract: Izabal (Spanish pronunciation: [isaˈβal]) is one of the 22 departments of Guatemala. Its coastal areas form part of the homeland of the Garifuna people.

gtm-ja.title: Jalapa Department
gtm-ja.extract: Jalapa is a department of Guatemala. It is located in the south east of the country with the seat and capital at the city of Jalapa.

gtm-ju.title: Jutiapa Department
gtm-ju.extract: Jutiapa Department is a department of Guatemala that borders along El Salvador and the Pacific Ocean. The capital is the city of Jutiapa.

gtm-pe.title: Petén Department
gtm-pe.extract: Petén (from the Itz'a, Noj Petén, 'Great Island') is a department of Guatemala. It is geographically the northernmost department of Guatemala, as well as the largest by area –  at 35,854 km2 (13,843 sq mi) it accounts for about one third of Guatemala's area.

gtm-pr.title: El Progreso Department
gtm-pr.extract: El Progreso (Spanish pronunciation: [el pɾoˈɣɾeso]) is a department in Guatemala. The departmental capital is Guastatoya.

gtm-qc.title: Quiché Department
gtm-qc.extract: Quiché (Spanish pronunciation: [kiˈtʃe]) is a department of Guatemala. It is in the heartland of the Kʼicheʼ (Quiché) people, one of the Maya peoples, to the north-west of Guatemala City.

gtm-qz.title: Quetzaltenango Department
gtm-qz.extract: Quetzaltenango is a department in the western highlands of Guatemala. The capital is the city of Quetzaltenango, the second largest city in Guatemala.

gtm-re.title: Retalhuleu Department
gtm-re.extract: Retalhuleu (Spanish pronunciation: [re.ta.luˈlew], Retalhuléu) is a department located in the south-west of Guatemala, extending from the mountains to the Pacific Ocean coast.  It has an area of 1856 km2.

gtm-sa.title: Sacatepéquez Department
gtm-sa.extract: Sacatepéquez (Spanish pronunciation: [sakateˈpekes]) is one of the 22 departments of Guatemala. The name comes from Sacatepéquez, a city from 21 November 1542, until 29 July 1773, when it was destroyed by the 1773 Guatemala earthquake.

gtm-sm.title: San Marcos Department
gtm-sm.extract:
San Marcos (Spanish pronunciation: [ˌsam ˈmaɾkos]) is a department in southwestern Guatemala, on the Pacific Ocean and along the western Guatemala–Mexico border.
The department's capital is the city of San Marcos.

gtm-so.title: Sololá Department
gtm-so.extract: Sololá is a department in the west of Guatemala. The capital is the city of Sololá.

gtm-sr.title: Santa Rosa Department, Guatemala
gtm-sr.extract: Santa Rosa (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈsanta ˈrosa]) is a department in Guatemala. The capital is Cuilapa.

gtm-su.title: Suchitepéquez Department
gtm-su.extract: Suchitepéquez (Spanish pronunciation: [sutʃiteˈpekes]) is one of the 22 departments of Guatemala. Its capital is Mazatenango.

gtm-to.title: Totonicapán Department
gtm-to.extract: Totonicapán is one of the 22 departments of Guatemala. The capital is the city of Totonicapán.

gtm-za.title: Zacapa Department
gtm-za.extract: Zacapa (Spanish pronunciation: [saˈkapa]) is one of the 22 departments of Guatemala. It lies in eastern Guatemala with its capital in the city of Zacapa, approximately 112 kilometers (70 miles) from Guatemala City.

hnd.title: Honduras
hnd.extract: Honduras, officially the Republic of Honduras, is a country in Central America. It is bordered to the west by Guatemala, to the southwest by El Salvador, to the southeast by Nicaragua, to the south by the Pacific Ocean at the Gulf of Fonseca, and to the north by the Gulf of Honduras, a large inlet of the Caribbean Sea.

hnd-at.title: Atlántida Department
hnd-at.extract: Atlántida (Spanish pronunciation: [aˈtlan.ti.ða], lit. 'Atlantis') is a department located on the north Caribbean shore of Honduras. The capital is the port city of La Ceiba.

hnd-ch.title: Choluteca Department
hnd-ch.extract: Choluteca is one of the 18 departments (departamentos) into which Honduras is divided. The departmental capital is the city of Choluteca.

hnd-cl.title: Colón Department (Honduras)
hnd-cl.extract: Colón is one of the 18 departments into which Honduras is divided. It was created in 1881.

hnd-cm.title: Comayagua Department
hnd-cm.extract: Comayagua (Spanish pronunciation: [komaˈʝaɣwa]) is one of the 18 departments (departamentos) into which Honduras is divided. The departmental capital is Comayagua.

hnd-cp.title: Copán Department
hnd-cp.extract: Copán is one of the departments in the western part of Honduras. The departmental capital is the town of Santa Rosa de Copán.

hnd-cr.title: Cortés Department
hnd-cr.extract: Cortés is one of the 18 departments of Honduras. The department covers an area of 3,954 km2 and, in 2015, had an estimated population of 1,612,762, making it the most populous in Honduras.

hnd-ep.title: El Paraíso Department
hnd-ep.extract:
El Paraíso (Spanish pronunciation: [el paɾaˈiso]) is one of the 18 departments (departamentos) into which Honduras is divided.
The territory of El Paraíso was initially part of the departments of Tegucigalpa (renamed Francisco Morazán in 1943) and Olancho after Central America gained its independence in 1825.

hnd-fm.title: Francisco Morazán Department
hnd-fm.extract:
Francisco Morazán (Spanish pronunciation: [fɾanˈsisko moɾaˈsan], abbreviated FMO) is one of the departments of Honduras.
It is located in the central part of the nation.

hnd-gd.title: Gracias a Dios Department
hnd-gd.extract: Gracias a Dios (Spanish pronunciation: [ˈɡɾasjas a ˈðjos]; "Thanks to God" or "Thank God") is one of the 18 departments (departamentos) into which Honduras is divided. The departmental capital is Puerto Lempira; and up until 1975 it was Brus Laguna.

hnd-ib.title: Bay Islands Department
hnd-ib.extract: The Bay Islands (Spanish: Islas de la Bahía; pronounced [ˈislas de la βaˈi.a]) is a group of islands off the Caribbean coast of Honduras. Collectively, the islands form one of the 18 departments of Honduras.

hnd-in.title: Intibucá Department
hnd-in.extract: Intibucá (Spanish pronunciation: [in.ti.βuˈka]) is one of the 18 departments in the Republic of Honduras. Intibucá covers a total surface area of 1,186.1 square miles (3,072 km2).

hnd-le.title: Lempira Department
hnd-le.extract: Lempira is one of the 18 departments—a territorial division roughly comparable to a U.S. state—in Honduras. located in the western part of the country, it is bordered by the departments of Ocotepeque and Copán to the west, Intibucá to the east, and Santa Bárbara to the north.

hnd-lp.title: La Paz Department (Honduras)
hnd-lp.extract: La Paz (Spanish pronunciation: [la pas]) is one of the 18 political and geographic departments of Honduras. The departmental capital is the city of La Paz.

hnd-oc.title: Ocotepeque Department
hnd-oc.extract: Ocotepeque is one of the 18 departments of Honduras, Central America, located in the West and bordering both El Salvador and Guatemala. It was formed in 1906 from part of Copán department.

hnd-ol.title: Olancho Department
hnd-ol.extract: Olancho is the largest of all the 18 departments into which Honduras is divided. The department covers a total surface area of 24,057 km2 (9,288 sq mi) and has an estimated 2015 population of 537,306 inhabitants.

hnd-sb.title: Santa Bárbara Department, Honduras
hnd-sb.extract: Santa Bárbara is one of the 18 departments (departamentos) into which Honduras is divided. The departmental capital is Santa Bárbara.

hnd-va.title: Valle Department
hnd-va.extract:
Valle is one of the 18 departments into which Honduras is divided.
The departmental capital is Nacaome.

hnd-yo.title: Yoro Department
hnd-yo.extract: Yoro is one of the 18 departments into which Honduras is divided. The department contains rich agricultural lands, concentrated mainly on the valley of the Aguan River and the Sula Valley, on opposite ends.

hti.title: Haiti
hti.extract: Haiti, officially the Republic of Haiti, is a country in the Caribbean on the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean Sea, east of Cuba and Jamaica and south of The Bahamas. It occupies the western side of the island, which it shares with the Dominican Republic.

hti-ar.title: Artibonite (department)
hti-ar.extract: Artibonite (French pronunciation: [aʁtibɔnit]; Haitian Creole: Latibonit) is one of the ten departments of Haiti located in central Haiti. With an area of 4,887 km2 it is Haiti's largest department.

hti-ce.title: Centre (department)
hti-ce.extract: Centre (French, pronounced [sɑ̃tʁ] ) or Sant (Haitian Creole; both meaning "Center") is the only landlocked department (French: départements; Haitian Creole: depatman) of Haiti, located in the center of the country along the border with the Dominican Republic. As of 2015, its estimated population was 746,236.

hti-ga.title: Grand'Anse (department)
hti-ga.extract: Grand'Anse (, French: [ɡʁɑ̃tɑ̃s]), Grandans or Grantans (Haitian Creole: [ɡɣãtãs]; both meaning "Big Cove") is one of the ten departments of Haiti. Its capital is Jérémie.

hti-nd.title: Nord (Haitian department)
hti-nd.extract: Nord (French, pronounced [nɔʁ] ) or Nò (Haitian Creole, pronounced [nɔ]; both meaning "North") is one of the ten departments of Haiti and located in northern Haiti. It has an area of 2,114.91 km2 (816.57 sq mi) and a population of 1,067,177 (2015).

hti-ne.title: Nord-Est (department)
hti-ne.extract: Nord-Est (French, pronounced [nɔʁɛst] ) or Nodès (Haitian Creole; both meaning "North East") is one of the ten departments of Haiti, located in northern Haiti. It has an area of 1,623 km2 (627 sq mi), making it the smallest of all the departments.

hti-ni.title: Nippes
hti-ni.extract: Nippes (French, pronounced [nip] ) or Nip (Haitian Creole) is one of the ten departments (the highest-level political subdivisions) of Haiti located in southern Haiti. It is the most recently created department, having been split from Grand'Anse in 2003.

hti-no.title: Nord-Ouest (department)
hti-no.extract: Nord-Ouest (French, pronounced [nɔʁwɛst] ) or Nòdwès (Haitian Creole; both meaning "North West") is one of the ten departments of Haiti as well as the northernmost one. It has an area of 2,102.88 km2 (811.93 sq mi) and a population of 728,807 (2015 Census).

hti-ou.title: Ouest (department)
hti-ou.extract: Ouest (French, pronounced [wɛst] ) or Lwès (Haitian Creole; both meaning "West") is one of the ten departments of Haiti. It is located in south-central Haiti, linking the Great-North and the Tiburon Peninsula.

hti-sd.title: Sud (department)
hti-sd.extract: Sud (French, pronounced [syd] ) or Sid (Haitian Creole; both meaning "South") is one of the ten departments of Haiti and located in southern Haiti. It has an area of 2,653.60 square kilometres (1,024.56 sq mi) and a population of 774,976.

hti-se.title: Sud-Est (department)
hti-se.extract: Sud-Est (French, pronounced [sydɛst] ) or Sidès (Haitian Creole; both meaning "South East") is one of the ten departments of Haiti located in southern Haiti. It has an area of 2,034.10 km2 and a population of 632,601 (2015).

jam.title: Jamaica
jam.extract: Jamaica is an island country in the Caribbean, covering 10,991 square kilometres (4,244 sq mi). It is the third-largest island in the Greater Antilles and the Caribbean, after Cuba and Hispaniola.

jam-01.title: Kingston Parish
jam-01.extract: Kingston Parish is one of the 14 Parishes of Jamaica. It is part of the amalgamated municipal unit of Kingston and St.

jam-02.title: Saint Andrew Parish, Jamaica
jam-02.extract: Saint Andrew (Jamaican Patois: Sint Anju) is a parish, situated in the southeast of Jamaica in the county of Surrey. It lies north, west and east of Kingston, and stretches into the Blue Mountains.

jam-03.title: Saint Thomas Parish, Jamaica
jam-03.extract: Saint Thomas (Jamaican Patois: Sen Tamas or Tahmas), once known as Saint Thomas in the East, is a suburban parish situated at the south eastern end of Jamaica, within the county of Surrey. It is the birthplace of Paul Bogle, designated in 1969 as one of Jamaica's seven National Heroes.

jam-04.title: Portland Parish
jam-04.extract: Portland (Jamaican Patois: Puotlan), with its capital town Port Antonio, is a parish located on Jamaica's northeast coast. It is situated to the north of St Thomas and to the east of St Mary in Surrey County.

jam-05.title: Saint Mary Parish, Jamaica
jam-05.extract: Saint Mary (Jamaican Patois: Sint Mieri) is a parish located in the northeast section of Jamaica. With a population of 114,227, it is one of Jamaica's smallest parishes, located in the county of Middlesex.

jam-06.title: Saint Ann Parish
jam-06.extract: Saint Ann (Jamaican Patois: Sint An) is the largest parish in Jamaica. It is situated on the north coast of the island, in the county of Middlesex, roughly halfway between the eastern and western ends of the island.

jam-07.title: Trelawny Parish
jam-07.extract: Trelawny (Jamaican Patois: Trilaani or Chrilaani) is a parish in the county of Cornwall in northwest Jamaica. Its capital is Falmouth.

jam-08.title: Saint James Parish, Jamaica
jam-08.extract: St. James is a suburban parish, located on the north-west end of the island of Jamaica in the county of Cornwall.

jam-09.title: Hanover Parish
jam-09.extract: Hanover (Jamaican Patois: Anuova) is a parish located on the northwestern tip of the island of Jamaica. It is a part of the county of Cornwall, bordered by St.

jam-10.title: Westmoreland Parish
jam-10.extract: Westmoreland (Jamaican Patois: Wesmolan) is the westernmost parish in Jamaica, on the south side of the island. It lies south of Hanover, southwest of Saint James, and northwest of Saint Elizabeth, in the county of Cornwall.

jam-11.title: Saint Elizabeth Parish
jam-11.extract: Saint Elizabeth (Jamaican Patois: Sint Elizabet) is one of Jamaica's largest parishes. It is located in the southwest of the island, in the county of Cornwall.

jam-12.title: Manchester Parish
jam-12.extract: The Parish of Manchester (Jamaican Patois: Manchesta) is a parish located in west-central Jamaica, in the county of Middlesex. Its capital, Mandeville, is a major business centre.

jam-13.title: Clarendon Parish, Jamaica
jam-13.extract: Clarendon (Jamaican Patois: Clarindan) is a parish in Jamaica. It is located on the south of the island, roughly halfway between the island's eastern and western ends.

jam-14.title: Saint Catherine Parish
jam-14.extract: Saint Catherine (Jamaican Patois: Sint Cyatrine) is a parish in the south east of Jamaica. It is located in the county of Middlesex, and is one of the island's largest and most economically valued parishes because of its many resources.

kna.title: Saint Kitts and Nevis
kna.extract: Saint Kitts and Nevis (SKN), officially the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis, is an island country located in the Caribbean consisting of the two islands of Saint Kitts and Nevis, in the Leeward Islands chain of the Lesser Antilles. With 261 square kilometres (101 sq mi) of territory, and roughly 48,000 inhabitants, it is the smallest sovereign state in the Western Hemisphere, in both area and population, as well as the world's smallest sovereign Federation.

kna-01.title: Christ Church Nichola Town Parish
kna-01.extract: Christ Church Nichola Town is one of the 14 administrative parishes that make up the Saint Kitts and Nevis. Christ Church Nichola Town is the fifth largest parish on Saint Kitts and is located on the east coast of the main island of Saint Kitts.

kna-02.title: Saint Anne Sandy Point Parish
kna-02.extract: Saint Anne Sandy Point is one of 14 administrative parishes that make up Saint Kitts and Nevis. It is the smallest parish on St.

kna-03.title: Saint George Basseterre Parish
kna-03.extract: Saint George Basseterre is one of 14 administrative parishes that make up Saint Kitts and Nevis. It is the largest parish on Saint Kitts and the second largest parish in Saint Kitts and Nevis (after Saint James Windward).

kna-04.title: Saint George Gingerland Parish
kna-04.extract: Saint George Gingerland, also known as Marketshop. St George parish in the southeastern part of the island of Nevis, Leeward Islands, West Indies.

kna-05.title: Saint James Windward Parish
kna-05.extract: Saint James Windward is the largest of five parishes on the island of Nevis. These five parishes are in turn part of the 14 administrative parishes making up the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

kna-06.title: Saint John Capisterre Parish
kna-06.extract: Saint John Capisterre is one of 14 administrative parishes that make up Saint Kitts and Nevis. It is the second largest parish on Saint Kitts (after Saint George Basseterre Parish), and the third largest parish in the federation (the largest being Saint James Windward Parish).

kna-07.title: Saint John Figtree Parish
kna-07.extract: Saint John Figtree is one of five administrative parishes which make up the small Caribbean island of Nevis. These five are part of the fourteen parishes that exist within the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis, a two-island country in the Leeward Islands, Lesser Antilles, West Indies.

kna-08.title: Saint Mary Cayon Parish
kna-08.extract: Saint Mary Cayon is one of 14 administrative parishes that make up Saint Kitts and Nevis. It is located on the main island of Saint Kitts and the parish capital is Cayon.

kna-09.title: Saint Paul Capisterre Parish
kna-09.extract: Saint Paul Capisterre is one of 14 administrative parishes that make up Saint Kitts and Nevis. It is the second smallest parish on St.

kna-10.title: Saint Paul Charlestown Parish
kna-10.extract: Saint Paul Charlestown is one of 14 administrative parishes that make up Saint Kitts and Nevis. It is located on the island of Nevis, and the parish capital is Charlestown, which is also capital of the entire island.

kna-11.title: Saint Peter Basseterre Parish
kna-11.extract: Saint Peter Basseterre is one of 14 administrative parishes that make up Saint Kitts and Nevis. It is located on the main island of Saint Kitts and the parish capital is Monkey Hill.

kna-12.title: Saint Thomas Lowland Parish
kna-12.extract: Saint Thomas Lowland is one of 5 Nevis parishes which are in turn part of the 14 administrative parishes that make up the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis. Leeward Islands, Lesser Antilles, West Indies.

kna-13.title: Saint Thomas Middle Island Parish
kna-13.extract: Saint Thomas Middle Island is one of 14 administrative parishes that make up Saint Kitts and Nevis. It is the third largest parish on the island of Saint Kitts, and fourth largest in the federation.

kna-14.title: Trinity Palmetto Point Parish
kna-14.extract: Trinity Palmetto Point is one of 14 administrative parishes that make up Saint Kitts and Nevis. It ranks 6th in terms of size of all the parishes on Saint Kitts.

lca.title: Saint Lucia
lca.extract: Saint Lucia (also written as St. Lucia) is an island country in the eastern and southern Caribbean.

lca-01.title: Anse la Raye District
lca-01.extract: Anse la Raye District is one of 10 districts (formerly called quarters) of the island nation of St. Lucia in the Caribbean Sea.

lca-02.title: Castries District
lca-02.extract: Castries District is one of 10 districts (formerly called quarters) of the Caribbean island nation of Saint Lucia. According to the 2012 census, the population of the district was 80,573, having shown a slow but steady increase over the past ten years.[1] The capital of Saint Lucia, the city of Castries, is located in this district.

lca-03.title: Choiseul District
lca-03.extract: Choiseul District is one of the 10 districts (formerly called quarter) of the Caribbean island nation of Saint Lucia.  Located on the southwestern side of the island, the district is home to 6,130 people, according to the 2019 census.

lca-04.title: Dauphin Quarter
lca-04.extract: Dauphin was a Quarter on the Caribbean island nation of Saint Lucia. The district was merged with Gros-Islet in 2014.

lca-05.title: Dennery District
lca-05.extract: Dennery District is one of 10 districts (formerly Quarters) of the Caribbean island nation of Saint Lucia.  The seat of Dennery District is the Dennery Village.

lca-06.title: Gros Islet District
lca-06.extract: Gros Islet District, one of 10 first order subdivision (districts, formerly quarters) of the Caribbean island nation of Saint Lucia which includes the island's northernmost point, Cap Point and the notable Cap Estate, where the renowned St. Lucia Golf and Country Club is located.

lca-07.title: Laborie District
lca-07.extract: Laborie District is a district of Saint Lucia.  According to the 2022 census, it had a population of 8,507 inhabitants.

lca-08.title: Micoud District
lca-08.extract: Micoud District is one of  10 districts (formerly called quarters) of the Caribbean island nation of Saint Lucia The seat of this district is the town of Micoud inside this district.  According to the 2002 census, the population of the district was 16,143 people.

lca-09.title: Praslin Quarter
lca-09.extract: Praslin Quarter was a former quarter  on the island nation of Saint Lucia.  Since at least 2001, it has been a second-order subdivision of the Micoud District.

lca-10.title: Soufrière District
lca-10.extract: Soufrière is a district on the Southwest coast of Saint Lucia in the West Indies. Soufrière was the former capital of Saint Lucia during times of French rule.

lca-11.title: Vieux Fort District
lca-11.extract: Vieux Fort is one of 10 districts of the Caribbean island country of Saint Lucia. Vieux Fort is also the name of the main town in the district.

maf.title: Collectivity of Saint Martin
maf.extract: The Collectivity of Saint Martin (French: Collectivité de Saint-Martin), commonly known as simply Saint Martin (Saint-Martin, [sɛ̃ maʁtɛ̃] ), is an overseas collectivity of France in the West Indies in the Caribbean, on the northern half of the island of Saint Martin, as well as some smaller adjacent islands. Saint Martin is separated from the island of Anguilla by the Anguilla Channel.

maf-x00.title: Collectivity of Saint Martin
maf-x00.extract: The Collectivity of Saint Martin (French: Collectivité de Saint-Martin), commonly known as simply Saint Martin (Saint-Martin, [sɛ̃ maʁtɛ̃] ), is an overseas collectivity of France in the West Indies in the Caribbean, on the northern half of the island of Saint Martin, as well as some smaller adjacent islands. Saint Martin is separated from the island of Anguilla by the Anguilla Channel.

mex.title: Mexico
mex.extract: Mexico, officially the United Mexican States, is a country in North America. It is the northernmost country in Latin America, bordering the United States of America to the north and Guatemala and Belize to the southeast, while having maritime boundaries with the Pacific Ocean to the west, the Caribbean Sea to the southeast, and the Gulf of Mexico to the east.

mex-agu.title: Aguascalientes
mex-agu.extract: Aguascalientes, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Aguascalientes, is one of the 32 states which comprise the federated entities of Mexico. At 22°N and with an average altitude of 1,950 m (6,400 ft) above sea level it is predominantly of semi-arid climate (Bhs and Bhk).

mex-bcn.title: Baja California
mex-bcn.extract: Baja California, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Baja California, is a state in Mexico. It is the northwesternmost of the 32 federal entities of Mexico.

mex-bcs.title: Baja California Sur
mex-bcs.extract: Baja California Sur, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Baja California Sur, is a state in Mexico. It is the 31st and last state to be admitted, in 1974.

mex-cam.title: Campeche
mex-cam.extract: Campeche, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Campeche, is one of the 31 states which, with Mexico City, make up the 32 federal entities of Mexico. Located in southeast Mexico, it is bordered by the states of Tabasco to the southwest, Yucatán to the northeast, Quintana Roo to the east, by the Petén department of Guatemala to the south, and by the Orange Walk District of Belize to the southeast.

mex-chh.title: Chihuahua (state)
mex-chh.extract: Chihuahua (Spanish pronunciation: [tʃiˈwawa] ), officially the Free and Sovereign State of Chihuahua is one of the 31 states which, along with Mexico City, are the 32 federal entities of Mexico. It is located in the northwestern part of Mexico and is bordered by the states of Sonora to the west, Sinaloa to the southwest, Durango to the south, and Coahuila to the east.

mex-chp.title: Chiapas
mex-chp.extract: Chiapas, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Chiapas, is one of the states that make up the 32 federal entities of Mexico. It comprises 124 municipalities as of September 2017 and its capital and largest city is Tuxtla Gutiérrez.

mex-coa.title: Coahuila
mex-coa.extract: Coahuila, formally Coahuila de Zaragoza, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Coahuila de Zaragoza, is one of the 31 states of Mexico. The largest city and state capital is the city of Saltillo; the second largest is Torreón and the third largest is Monclova (a former state capital); the fourth largest is Piedras Negras; and the fifth largest is Ciudad Acuña.

mex-col.title: Colima
mex-col.extract: Colima, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Colima, is among the 31 states that make up the 32 federated entities of Mexico. It shares its name with its capital and main city, Colima.

mex-dif.title: Mexico City
mex-dif.extract: Mexico City is the capital and  largest city of Mexico, as well as the most populous city in North America. It is one of the world's leading cultural and financial centers and, according to the Globalization and World Cities Research Network's 2024 ranking, is classified as an Alpha world city.

mex-dur.title: Durango
mex-dur.extract: Durango, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Durango, is one of the states which make up the 32 federal entities of Mexico, situated in the northwest portion of the country. With a population of 1,832,650, the eighth lowest of Mexico's states, Durango has Mexico's second-lowest population density, after Baja California Sur.

mex-gro.title: Guerrero
mex-gro.extract: Guerrero, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Guerrero, is one of the 31 states that compose the 32 Federal Entities of Mexico. It is divided into 85 municipalities.

mex-gua.title: Guanajuato
mex-gua.extract: Guanajuato, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Guanajuato, is one of the 32 states that make up the Federal Entities of Mexico. It is divided into 46 municipalities and its capital city is Guanajuato.

mex-hid.title: Hidalgo (state)
mex-hid.extract: Hidalgo, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Hidalgo, is one of the 31 states which, along with Mexico City, constitute the 32 federal entities of Mexico. It is divided into 84 municipalities and its capital city is Pachuca de Soto.

mex-jal.title: Jalisco
mex-jal.extract: Jalisco, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Jalisco, is one of the 31 states which, along with Mexico City, comprise the 32 Federal Entities of Mexico. It is located in western Mexico and is bordered by six states, Nayarit, Zacatecas, Aguascalientes, Guanajuato, Michoacán, and Colima.

mex-mex.title: State of Mexico
mex-mex.extract: The State of Mexico, officially Mexico, is one of the 32 federal entities of the United Mexican States. Sharing its name with both the country and the national capital, Mexico City, the state is colloquially distinguished as Edomex ([eðoˈmeks], from E[sta]do [de] Méx[ico], "State of Mexico").

mex-mic.title: Michoacán
mex-mic.extract: Michoacán, formally Michoacán de Ocampo, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Michoacán de Ocampo, is one of the 31 states which, together with Mexico City, compose the Federal Entities of Mexico. The state is divided into 113 municipalities and its capital city is Morelia (formerly called Valladolid).

mex-mor.title: Morelos
mex-mor.extract: Morelos, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Morelos, is a landlocked state located in south-central Mexico. It is one of the 32 states which comprise the Federal Entities of Mexico.

mex-nay.title: Nayarit
mex-nay.extract: Nayarit, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Nayarit, is one of the 31 states that, along with Mexico City, comprise the Federal Entities of Mexico. It is divided in 20 municipalities and its capital city is Tepic.

mex-nle.title: Nuevo León
mex-nle.extract: Nuevo León, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Nuevo León, is a state in northeastern Mexico. The state borders the Mexican states of Tamaulipas, Coahuila, Zacatecas, and San Luis Potosi, and has an extremely narrow international border with the U.S. state of Texas.

mex-oax.title: Oaxaca
mex-oax.extract: Oaxaca, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Oaxaca, is one of the 31 states of Mexico. It is divided into 570 municipalities, of which 418 (almost three quarters) are governed by the system of usos y costumbres (customs and traditions) with recognized local forms of self-governance.

mex-pue.title: Puebla
mex-pue.extract: Puebla, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Puebla, is one of the 31 states that, along with Mexico City, comprise the Federal Entities of Mexico. It is divided into 217 municipalities and its capital is Puebla City.

mex-que.title: Querétaro
mex-que.extract: Querétaro, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Querétaro, is one of the 32 federal entities of Mexico. It is divided into 18 municipalities.

mex-roo.title: Quintana Roo
mex-roo.extract: Quintana Roo, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Quintana Roo, is one of the 31 states which, along with Mexico City, constitute the 32 federal entities of Mexico. It is divided into 11 municipalities, and its capital city is Chetumal.

mex-sin.title: Sinaloa
mex-sin.extract: Sinaloa (Spanish pronunciation: [sinaˈloa] ), officially the Free and Sovereign State of Sinaloa, is one of the 31 states which, along with Mexico City, compose the Federal Entities of Mexico. It is divided into 20 municipalities, and its capital and largest city is Culiacán Rosales.

mex-slp.title: San Luis Potosí
mex-slp.extract: San Luis Potosí, officially the Free and Sovereign State of San Luis Potosí, is one of the 32 states which compose the Federal Entities of Mexico. It is divided in 59 municipalities and is named after its capital city, San Luis Potosí.

mex-son.title: Sonora
mex-son.extract: Sonora (Spanish pronunciation: [soˈnoɾa] ), officially the Free and Sovereign State of Sonora, is one of the 31 states which, along with Mexico City, comprise the Federal Entities of Mexico. The state is divided into 72 municipalities.

mex-tab.title: Tabasco
mex-tab.extract: Tabasco, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Tabasco, is one of the 32 federal entities of Mexico. It is divided into 17 municipalities and its capital city is Villahermosa.

mex-tam.title: Tamaulipas
mex-tam.extract: Tamaulipas, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Tamaulipas, is a state in Mexico; it is one of the 31 states which, along with Mexico City, comprise the 32 federated entities of Mexico. It is divided into 43 municipalities.

mex-tla.title: Tlaxcala
mex-tla.extract: Tlaxcala, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Tlaxcala, is one of the 32 federal entities that comprise the Federal Entities of Mexico. It is divided into 60 municipalities and the capital city and the largest city is Tlaxcala de Xicohténcatl.

mex-ver.title: Veracruz
mex-ver.extract: Veracruz, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Veracruz de Ignacio de la Llave, is one of the 31 states that, along with Mexico City, comprise the 32 Federal Entities of Mexico. Located in eastern Mexico, it is bordered by seven states: Tamaulipas, San Luis Potosí, Hidalgo, Puebla, Oaxaca, Chiapas, and Tabasco.

mex-yuc.title: Yucatán
mex-yuc.extract: Yucatán, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Yucatán, is one of the 31 states which, along with Mexico City, constitute the 32 federal entities of Mexico. It comprises 106 separate municipalities.

mex-zac.title: Zacatecas
mex-zac.extract: Zacatecas, officially the Free and Sovereign State of Zacatecas, is one of the 31 states of Mexico. It is divided into 58 municipalities and its capital city is Zacatecas.

msr.title: Montserrat
msr.extract: Montserrat ( MONT-sə-RAT, locally ) is a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean. It is part of the Leeward Islands, the northern portion of the Lesser Antilles chain of the West Indies.

msr-a.title: Montserrat
msr-a.extract: Montserrat ( MONT-sə-RAT, locally ) is a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean. It is part of the Leeward Islands, the northern portion of the Lesser Antilles chain of the West Indies.

msr-g.title: Saint George, Barbados
msr-g.extract: St. George is a parish of Barbados.

msr-p.title: Montserrat
msr-p.extract: Montserrat ( MONT-sə-RAT, locally ) is a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean. It is part of the Leeward Islands, the northern portion of the Lesser Antilles chain of the West Indies.

mtq.title: Martinique
mtq.extract: Martinique ( MAR-tin-EEK, French pronunciation: [maʁtinik] ; Martinican Creole: Matinik or Matnik; Kalinago: Madinina or Madiana) is an island in the Lesser Antilles of the West Indies, in the eastern Caribbean Sea. A part of the French West Indies (Antilles), Martinique is an overseas department and region and a single territorial collectivity of France.

mtq-mq.title: Martinique
mtq-mq.extract: Martinique ( MAR-tin-EEK, French pronunciation: [maʁtinik] ; Martinican Creole: Matinik or Matnik; Kalinago: Madinina or Madiana) is an island in the Lesser Antilles of the West Indies, in the eastern Caribbean Sea. A part of the French West Indies (Antilles), Martinique is an overseas department and region and a single territorial collectivity of France.

nic.title: Nicaragua
nic.extract: Nicaragua, officially the Republic of Nicaragua, is a country in Central America, comprising 130,370 square kilometers (50,340 sq mi).
